note: Generic line layout. Zone IDs are referenced by every defect in defects.json. Replace typical values with your line's actual setpoints before using this on a real line.
diagram: images/candidates/km_sheetline_labeled-04.png + -05.png (KraussMaffei sheet line, labeled; PC lines add the dryer, gear pump and UV co-extruder)

Z1.name: Resin drying and feeding
Z1.typical: PC dried at about 120 °C for at least 4 h, dew point -40 °C or lower, target moisture below 0.02 %

Z2.name: Main extruder
parts: vacuum vent (degassing port) and vacuum pump
Z2.typical: Melt temperature roughly 270-310 °C depending on grade

Z3.name: Melt filtration
Z3.typical: Watch the pressure difference across the screen; rising difference means the screen is loading up

Z4.name: Gear pump (melt pump)
Z4.typical: Stable inlet pressure means stable output

Z5.name: UV co-extruder and feedblock
Z5.typical: Thin UV-protective cap layer on one or both surfaces

Z6.name: Flat sheet die
parts: flexible lip and lip adjustment bolts
Z6.typical: Lip gap set slightly above final thickness; die zones balanced across width

Z7.name: Polishing roll stack (3-roll calender)
parts: melt bank in the first nip
Z7.typical: Roll temperatures roughly 100-140 °C (below PC glass transition, about 147 °C)

Z8.name: Cooling conveyor (roller table)
Z8.typical: Sheet must cool evenly top and bottom

Z9.name: Edge trim
Z9.typical: PC is notch-sensitive; trim while the sheet is still warm enough

Z10.name: Protective film laminator
Z10.typical: Even tension and nip pressure across width

Z11.name: Haul-off (pull rolls)
Z11.typical: Small, stable speed ratio relative to the roll stack

Z12.name: Cross-cut saw and stacker
Z12.typical: Sharp blade, correct feed rate, sheet not too cold at cutting

safety: Barrel, adapter and die run at about 300 °C and molten PC causes severe burns: heat-resistant gloves, sleeves and face shield for any work at Z2-Z6.
Never reach into the roll stack nip (Z7), the laminator nip (Z10) or the haul-off (Z11) while running. These are crushing and draw-in points.
Die lip cleaning while running only with brass tools, only if your plant procedure allows it, and only by trained operators. Never use steel tools on die lips or polishing rolls.
Screen changes and any opening of the melt path follow the plant procedure: melt under pressure can spray.
Saw (Z12) and edge-trim knives (Z9): lockout/tagout before touching blades.
If in doubt, stop and call the shift lead or maintenance. The assistant gives guidance; it does not replace plant procedures.
